kit: kit_v2_2 (kit_v2_1 with the two torches changed; the other 10 meshes are byte-identical copies of kit_v2_1)
style: Look B (chunky low-poly, flat warm colours, palette texture)

conventions.origin: base centre at ground level (see per-mesh pivot notes)
conventions.texture: kit_palette 256px palette PNG, per-vertex UVs at palette cell centres, no vertex colours (each FBX has its own copy of the png embedded + beside it)
conventions.scenery: ALL meshes are scenery: CanCollide = false
conventions.fbx: Blender export, axis_forward=-Z axis_up=Y, global_scale 1, object_types MESH+EMPTY

lights_howto: Each light FBX contains (a) an Empty/Null node named LightAttach and (b) a separate mesh object <mesh>_Glow with its own material <mesh>_glow_mat. In Roblox set the <mesh>_Glow MeshPart Material=Neon (colour 255,190,110) and add a PointLight (Color 255,170,90) to an Attachment named LightAttach at the listed position. NOTE: whether Studio import converts the FBX Null into an Attachment automatically is not verified here; positions are given in Roblox coordinates so a script can create the Attachment if it does not. Torch _Glow part has two colours (255,170,90 tongues, 255,220,150 core) from the palette texture. (kit_v2_2: the torches now use _Flame and _Core parts instead of _Glow; the lanterns still use <mesh>_Glow with the palette texture.)

rock_tones_rgb.note: kit_ruin_arch, kit_ruin_wall and kit_boulder_pile use ONLY these three palette cells for stone (identical to cave v2.2 and kit_v1_2 rocks); moss caps use the kit_v1 LeafGreen/LeafDk/LeafLt greens

kit_boulder_pile.pivot_note: 4 boulders (3 stacked, 1 leaning), moss caps, 5 fern tufts. Lowest point exactly y=-2 (base sunk 2 studs); origin x/z centre, y=0 is ground level.

kit_canopy_wall.pivot_note: Closed solid curtain, uneven top with 4 palm-crown bumps, tapered scalloped bottom; base-centre origin, min y=0.

kit_cliff_ridge.pivot_note: Rounded rock ridge (115,100,92) cave-rock tones with green tops, closed with skirts to y=0.

kit_crate_stack.pivot_note: 3 crates (1 open, spilling coconuts), 2 barrels, rope coil, canvas tarp half pulled off to the -X side.

kit_hut_leanto.pivot_note: Open-sided lean-to, open front faces +Z, slanted palm-thatch roof, hammock, plank shelf with 2 bottles. Origin base centre at ground.

kit_lantern_hanging.pivot_note: PIVOT IS THE TOP OF THE RING (y=0, ring top). The lantern hangs BELOW the pivot: model spans y -3.2..0. Hang it from a rope/hinge at the pivot.

kit_lantern_post.pivot_note: Crooked wooden post with crossbar and brace; lantern hangs from the crossbar 3.4 studs toward +X. Origin = post base centre at ground.

kit_rowboat_broken.pivot_note: Hull split along the side, tipped on its side in sand drifts, faded paint (90,140,150) on planks, one oar upright, one cracked on the ground. About 20 long (X).

kit_ruin_arch.pivot_note: Broken arch, left pillar standing, right side collapsed into rubble pile (+X), moss caps, vine strip draped over arch.

kit_ruin_wall.pivot_note: Wall chunk variant with window gap, buttress, rubble, moss caps. About 23 wide incl. rubble (wall body ~20).

kit_torch_tiki.pivot_note: Bamboo pole, rope wraps, low bowl, origin base centre (unchanged). Flame = 3 tongues (_Flame), Core = pale inner core (_Core), both plain Neon colour parts; LightAttach at the flame centre.

kit_torch_tiki_short.pivot_note: Bamboo pole, rope wraps, low bowl, origin base centre (unchanged). Flame = 3 tongues (_Flame), Core = pale inner core (_Core), both plain Neon colour parts; LightAttach at the flame centre.

deviations: hut is about 32 wide x 27 tall x 30 deep (spec 30x25), ruin_wall about 23 wide incl. rubble, boulder_pile 31x19 (17.3 above ground), crate_stack 20x12.5 (spec 18x14), rowboat 20 long x 14 tall (on its side)
LightAttach is a plain Empty exported as an FBX Null; Roblox import behaviour unverified
v2_1_changes: kit_canopy_wall: uneven top line, 4 taller palm-crown bumps (tall narrow dome + fan domes) rising to ~1.5-2x the line height, bottom tapered (thickness 10 -> 3.2) with a scalloped lower edge instead of a flat slab; still a closed solid (double sided).

kit_torch_tiki / _short: teardrop flame of 3 orange tongues Flame (255,170,90) around a taller brighter core FlameCore (255,220,150), both in the separate <mesh>_Glow object; bowl rim lowered to 0.62 above the pole top so the flame stands well above it; LightAttach moved to the flame centre.
kit_cliff_ridge: peaks rounded (cosine profile, less noise), rock warmed to Rock (115,100,92) with RockDk (94,82,76) / RockLt (135,119,110) banding, far more green on top (RidgeGreen).
palette_note: Torch Flame palette cell is (255,140,50) (was 255,170,90 in v2_1); the torch Flame/Core objects no longer sample the palette. Unchanged meshes keep their v2_1 palette/UVs.
v2_2_changes: Torch _Glow part split into two objects: <mesh>_Flame (the 3 tongues) and <mesh>_Core (pale inner core), each with its own material and NO texture node (plain Base Color/Emission colour only). UVs are still exported on both.
Core made larger (radius 0.5 -> 0.78 relative) so it shows between and above the tongues; its tip stays just under the tallest tongue so sizes, pivot and LightAttach are unchanged.
neon_howto: In Studio: set <mesh>_Flame to Material=Neon, Color=(255,140,50) and <mesh>_Core to Material=Neon, Color=(255,220,150), and clear TextureID on both (no texture is used). Body part keeps the palette texture. PointLight colour (255,170,90) on the LightAttach Attachment.
note: kit_v2_6_1: texture-only change for kit_ruin_wall (geometry identical: verts, tris, smoothing, bounds, 11056 tris; only 3920 of 5702 UVs re-pointed to wall-only cells). Other kit files byte-identical to kit_v2_6.

HutWoodDk idx62 (new, hut only).note: 56 hut verts that used WoodDk idx35 (86,54,32) re-pointed here; WoodDk cell unchanged for crate_stack/rowboat_broken/lantern_post

hut_palette_change.Flame/FlameCore idx60,61: filled in hut PNG (62-colour palette layout); unused by hut

ruin_wall.pivot: bbox mode, same as v2: x/z centred, y min = 0
ruin_wall.fit: per-axis fit to the v2 bbox (factors x1.002 y0.953 z1.000, all within 5%)
ruin_wall.style: rounded boxes (5x5 grid per face pushed onto a bevelled box), low-frequency noise + per-vertex jitter, per-stone rotation (+-4.5 yaw, +-2.8 roll, +-1.6 pitch), width/height/depth jitter, +-0.12/0.18 offsets, smooth shading; RockDk core slab behind each course so crevices read as shadow
ruin_wall.colours: Rock (115,100,92) main, RockDk (94,82,76) darker, RockLt (135,119,110) light; chosen by low-frequency noise, never an ABAB checker; moss caps LeafLt (96,176,80)/LeafGreen (62,150,72); vines/ferns unchanged cells. No new palette cells.
ruin_wall.uv: one palette-cell centre UV per colour group (same convention as the other kit meshes); wall PNG is the kit palette PNG
ruin_wall.palette_png_note: kit_ruin_wall.png is built from the current kit_lib palette (v2_4 values: StrawDk (166,134,74), StrawLt (222,190,130), HutWoodDk at idx 62); rock/moss cells are unchanged vs v2_4

ruin_wall_cells.RockDk idx(unchanged) (94,82,76): now ONLY the 8 hidden dark core slabs behind the courses (kept dark, unchanged)
ruin_wall_cells.unchanged: all other cells in the wall PNG incl. Rock/RockDk/RockLt, moss, vine, fern; every other mesh keeps its own PNG and cells (byte-identical)

why_preview_dark.cause: Render, not the texture cells. The Workbench preview (STUDIO light, shadows on, world (0.55,0.68,0.80), default Blender view transform, no exposure/look set in render_kit22.py) darkens and desaturates every colour: beach sand (226,184,128) renders (131,120,104) (x0.58), hut straw (200,165,90) renders about (150,130,94), and lit wall stone (115,100,92) renders about (72,64,56) (x0.63); stone in shade renders (40,34,31).
why_preview_dark.not_the_cause: The dark gap cores: they are separate hidden slabs (8) behind the courses, and the visible stone faces already mapped to Rock (115,100,92), RockDk (94,82,76) and RockLt (135,119,110). The v2_6_1 preview pixels at the same spots are within +-3 of v2_6.
why_preview_dark.implication: Studio will not show ~(60,55,55); the cells are already the target warm greys. If a brighter preview is wanted, change the render (exposure / Standard view transform), not the PNG.
